sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 1052.2 ± 92.8 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: HA-tagging did not affect processing, glycosylation, or localisation of ELTD1 (L7); cell-surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells with anti-HA-APC antibody (L3, L4); G protein coupling (NanoBiT complementation) assays performed on HA-tagged full-length receptor (L1, L2); N-terminal HA+GFP cassette showed no negative effect on cell-surface expression levels (L12).
sites.rationale: The signal peptide spans residues 1–19 (last residue T19); the mature N-terminus begins at Q20. An HA tag inserted after residue 19 is placed on the extracellular face, well upstream of TM1 (residues 433–453), giving >400 residues of clearance. Python confirmed seq[18]='T' and seq[19]='Q'. L7 explicitly states HA-tagging of full-length, membrane-anchored ELTD1/ADGRL4 did not affect processing, glycosylation, or localisation; L3/L4/L5 confirm surface display by flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells; L1/L2 show G protein coupling assays were successfully performed on the same HA-tagged construct, establishing functional tolerance. Full-length, membrane-anchored ADGRL4/ELTD1 was stably expressed in HUVECs via lentiviral transduction with an HA tag placed immediately after the native signal peptide (cleavage after residue 19, mature N-terminus Q20). Anti-HA-Alexa Fluor 488 staining and confocal microscopy confirmed cell-surface display. The same N-terminal HA placement is independently used in PMC12830901 (flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells with G protein coupling assays) and PMC12971276 (multifunctional N-terminal cassette including HA + GFP downstream of the signal peptide, no negative effect on cell-surface expression levels).

sources.claim: HA‐tagging of ELTD1 did not affect processing, glycosylation or localisation of ELTD1 (Sheldon et al., 2021 ).

literature_notes: All ledger lines (L1–L13) converge on a single extracellular tag site: the N-terminal HA (and in L10/L13, HA+GFP) epitope placed immediately after the signal peptide cleavage site (after residue 19). No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any of the short extracellular loops (ECL1: 496–499, ECL2: 554–573, ECL3: 640–646) or in the large ectodomain at an internal position. The C-terminal SmBiT (L1/L2) and FLAG (L11) tags are placed at the cytoplasmic C-terminus (residues 668–690, intracellular per topology), so they are recorded in other_positions. L9 describes tagged and untagged constructs used for functional signalling studies but does not specify the tag position beyond 'N-terminal', consistent with the same site; it was not used as the primary supporting clip because L7 is more explicit about tolerance. L13 names an HA- and GFP-tagged aGPCR cell line but does not add a new junction beyond what L10 already establishes.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal SmBiT complementation fragment tethered via a 12-aa GS linker to the cytoplasmic C-terminus of full-length ADGRL4; residues 668–690 are intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface epitope site.

C-terminal FLAG tag used for flow cytometry detection and FLAG-Trap purification; placed at the intracellular C-terminus (668–690 intracellular per topology), not accessible from the extracellular face.
